## Relación entre $n$ y precisión del IC

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-align: center
library(ggplot2)
sigma <- 0.8
ns    <- 10:200
df_amp <- data.frame(
  n    = rep(ns, 2),
  amp  = c(2*1.96*sigma/sqrt(ns), 2*2.576*sigma/sqrt(ns)),
  conf = rep(c("95%","99%"), each = length(ns))
)
ggplot(df_amp, aes(x = n, y = amp, color = conf)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.3) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.4, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray50", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = 185, y = 0.43,
           label = "objetivo: ±0.2 kg", color = "gray40",
           size = 4, fontface = "italic") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("95%" = "#1e3a8a","99%" = "#991b1b")) +
  labs(x = "Tamaño de muestra n",
       y = "Amplitud del IC (millones/empresa)",
       title = "Amplitud del IC para ventas del sector comercio (σ = 0.8 kg) según n y nivel de confianza",
       color = "Confianza") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"))
```
